title: Call Me Hand Emoji 🤙 Meaning: Shaka, Hang Loose and Calls
description: 🤙 is both the “call me” phone gesture and the Hawaiian shaka for hang loose. Find out what the call me hand emoji means in texts, surf culture and slang.
summary: The 🤙 call me hand emoji has two main meanings. Held to the ear, the thumb-and-pinky shape mimics a phone: call me. Waved loosely, it is the shaka, the Hawaiian gesture for hang loose, thanks, take it easy and friendly goodwill. In slang it also means “sounds good” or “cool.”
meaning: Unicode named it for the telephone mime, and people do use it that way: “🤙 when you land” or “give me a 🤙 later.” The gesture imitates an old handset, thumb at the ear and little finger at the mouth. Younger people who grew up with flat smartphones tend to mime a call with a flat palm, yet the emoji's phone meaning is still widely understood.

The shaka is the richer meaning. In Hawaii it is an everyday sign of aloha, used to say hello, thank you, no worries or right on, and drivers flash it when someone lets them merge. A commonly told origin story traces it to Hamana Kalili, a sugar mill worker from Laie who lost three middle fingers in an accident, though accounts differ. Surfers carried the sign to beaches around the world.

From surf culture it moved into general slang for relaxed approval. “Sounds good 🤙” is easygoing agreement, cooler in tone than a thumbs up. In Brazil the gesture is common well beyond the beach and is tied to surf and jiu-jitsu communities. Fans of several college teams in the United States use it too, and it is a staple of skate, snowboard and van-life captions.

Some regional meanings differ. In parts of the Caribbean, Australia and Russia, tilting the thumb toward the mouth with the same handshape suggests having a drink, so 🤙 can be an invitation for beers. In China the hand shape stands for the number six, which in turn carries slang praise meaning “smooth” or “awesome.”

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Either an instruction to phone someone or a relaxed sign-off. “Call me 🤙” is literal. “See you Saturday 🤙” is the shaka: all good, looking forward to it. As a one-emoji reply, it says “cool, got it” with a laid-back flavor. Men use it frequently with each other as an unfussy way to confirm plans.

contexts.label: In surf and outdoor culture
contexts.body: Beach photos, wave reports, hiking shots and camping trips attract it naturally. It signals stoke and gratitude for a good day outside. Brands in surfing, skating and adventure travel lean on it heavily. In Hawaii-related posts it carries real local meaning, expressing aloha spirit rather than just holiday mood.

contexts.label: From a crush or date
contexts.body: After exchanging numbers, 🤙 can be a mildly flirty “call me,” especially with a wink. More often it is simply friendly. If someone replies to your date suggestion with it, they are agreeing in a casual way. It shows interest in the plan, though not necessarily strong romantic feeling.

Call me; removes doubt that the phone meaning is intended.
Laid-back cool; everything is under control.

confusedWith.difference: 🤘 raises the index and little fingers for rock on. 🤙 extends the thumb and little finger for the shaka or a phone call. Horns are loud and intense, while the shaka is mellow and friendly.
🤟 extends thumb, index and little finger, the sign for “I love you.” 🤙 leaves the index finger down. One declares affection, and the other says take it easy or call me.
📞 is an actual phone handset, used for calls, contact details and customer service. 🤙 is a hand gesture that can mean “call me” but more often conveys a casual attitude.

avoid: Do not use it to close a serious or apologetic message, where its breeziness seems careless.
Avoid it in formal work communication; it is beach-casual in tone.
Do not count on the “call me” meaning alone when a call is important; write it out.
design: A hand with the thumb and little finger extended and the three middle fingers curled into the palm. Depending on the platform it is shown from the front or the back and tilted at different angles, which nudges it toward either the phone mime or the shaka. It was added in 2016 and supports skin tones.

faqs.a: Either “call me” or “hang loose.” As a sign-off or reply it usually means cool, sounds good or thanks, in a relaxed tone. If phone calls are being discussed, it is the literal call gesture.

faqs.q: What does 🤙 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Most of the time, casual agreement or friendliness, the equivalent of “right on, man.” If you just gave him your number, he may be saying he will call. It is generally easygoing, not intense.

The shaka is a Hawaiian hand gesture with thumb and pinky extended, often given a slight shake. It expresses aloha: friendliness, gratitude and a take-it-easy outlook. Surfers spread it globally, and the emoji is its usual digital form.

It is a popular positive gesture meaning cool, all good or thanks, tied to surf and beach culture and known there as “hang loose.” Brazilian athletes, jiu-jitsu practitioners included, use it constantly in photos and posts.

faqs.q: Is 🤙 the same as the number six in China?
faqs.a: The hand shape is how many Chinese speakers show six on one hand. Because “666” is internet slang for something impressively skilled, 🤙 can carry that praise in Chinese-language chats, a meaning unrelated to phones or surfing.
